chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), regarding
a man who broke the hand of a man, then the hand of the man was cured. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no retaliation regarding this, but he would be given the compensation (Arsh).'

key_terms.قِصَاص: Retaliation in kind (exact retribution for injury)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qisas and Arsh in cases of healed bodily injury according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between Qisas (exact retaliation) and Arsh (fixed monetary compensation) in cases of bodily injury, specifically ruling that complete healing of the limb precludes Qisas but necessitates Arsh. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle that Qisas requires the injury to be identical in kind and degree, whereas Arsh serves as a flexible compensation for the loss of function or value. The ruling underscores the Prophet's and Imams' emphasis on justice and restorative equity in personal injury cases.
